title: Migrating Homebrew to a new Mac

entries.query_str: new mac (apple silicon) from an older apple silicon one. best way to move homebrew stuff without migration assistant copying junk
entries.answer:
Use a **Brewfile** to reinstall cleanly instead of copying `/opt/homebrew` [1][2]:

On the old Mac:
```bash
brew bundle dump --file=~/Brewfile --describe
```
Review the file and delete anything you no longer use. Copy it over (AirDrop, iCloud, git dotfiles repo).

On the new Mac:
```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
brew bundle --file=~/Brewfile
```
This installs formulae, casks and (optionally) Mac App Store apps listed via `mas` [1]. Things a Brewfile won't move: config files (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.ssh` — copy those deliberately), language-version managers' installed versions (pyenv/nvm), and app-specific settings [2].

entries.query_str: ssh keys — copy or make new ones
entries.answer: Either is fine; many people **generate new keys per machine** (`ssh-keygen -t ed25519`), add them to GitHub, and revoke the old machine's key when it's retired — so a lost or sold laptop can't access anything [1]. Copying `~/.ssh` works too, but then the same key lives on two machines.
